title: When Shall Thy Love Constrain
description: When Shall Thy Love Constrain in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 12 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 137. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When shall thy love con-strain, And force me to thy breast? When shall my soul re-turn a-gain To her e-ter-nal rest?

lines: And force me to thy breast?
When shall my soul return again
Thou hast the words of endless life;
It calls me still to seek thy face,
And stoops to ask my love.
Lord, at thy feet I fall!
I groan to be set free;
I fain would now obey the call,
And give up all for thee.
Thou didst with all things part;
Didst lead a suffering life below,
The God of all that breathe
Was found in fashion as a man,
To tear my soul from earth away,
Nay, but I yield, I yield!
I can hold out no more,
I sink, by dying love compelled,
Settle and fix my wavering soul
With all thy weight of love.
To seek and taste no other bliss
My hope, my heavenly treasure, now

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
